text:
maria: quick q about message/schema for streaming deltas + tool/function call args. i opened PR #4123 with a proposal to normalize arg keys to snake_case and put final args under `tool_call.params`. worried about compatibility with existing client libs. thoughts?

dom: do we have to canonicalize casing on the wire? some of our clients (mobile/web) expect camelCase. maybe we surface both but document one canonical form?

kevin: +1 on having a canonical server-side shape. my preference is to keep the runtime emitting a single canonical field (e.g., `tool_call`) and provide a lightweight compatibility layer in the client SDKs for casing. that keeps server code simpler.

ashley: backward-compat note: older integrations still look for `function_call` as the key (not `tool_call`). can we alias the key transparently at parse time? otherwise we'll break a bunch of downstream consumers.

maria: aliasing sounds reasonable. plan: server will accept `function_call` or `tool_call` inbound and normalize to internal `tool_call`. outbound we emit canonical `tool_call`. i'll add an aliasing layer in PR. also thinking about streaming deltas for params: do we send param diffs, full partials, or path-based patches?

kevin: for streaming, prefer delta events that include partial param updates and a final commit event with full `params`. e.g. small guids:
```json
{"delta": {"tool_call": {"name": "search", "params_delta": {"query": "foo"}}}}
...
{"event": "tool_call_end", "tool_call": {"name": "search", "params": {"query": "foo", "filters": []}}}
```
this way receivers can incrementally render args and also verify final state.

dom: agree. also needs a clear error model for streaming aborts: if stream cuts out, do we emit a `tool_call_error` or a final `tool_call_end` with `status: partial`? my vote: emit explicit `tool_call_abort` with diagnostic code + raw_bytes if any.

ashley: +1 for explicit abort event. and add a metric label so we can count partial tool_call completions in the console.

maria: protocol items i plan to add to PR:
- accept both `function_call` and `tool_call` inbound, normalize server-side
- emit `tool_call` outward only
- streaming shape: `params_delta` events + final `tool_call_end` with full `params`
- explicit `tool_call_abort` with diagnostics on truncated streams
- tests for camelCase/snake_case handling + examples in migration doc

ashley: small nit: nested param keys — do we canonicalize nested keys too? e.g., `userId` -> `user_id` inside `metadata` objects. would be a pain but better to be consistent.

kevin: yeah normalize nested keys when we canonicalize. add a header or envelope field to opt out for legacy bilateral integrations (`X-Redwood-Allow-legacy-casing: true`).

maria: good idea. i'll add opt-out header + writeup in docs. also adding two unit tests to PR: one for streaming delta ordering, one for legacy header behavior. assigning reviewers: @kevin @ashley @dom. can y'all take a look? aiming for EOD review so we can merge and cut a minor compat release.

sre-bot: deploy-check: rolling canary tests will run on merge. make sure the canary suite includes legacy consumer smoke.

dom: skimmed PR, left comment about meters and event_type — prefer `tool_delta` as instrumentation event_type so we can differentiate token-level deltas vs final tool_call.

kevin: LGTM pending the tests and one doc paragraph about why we prefer canonical snake_case.

ashley: added a comment on line 128 about base64 encoding for binary param values — we should reserve a convention like `{ "__attachment": {"encoding":"base64","mimetype":"image/png","data":"..."}}`. avoids confusion.

maria: perfect. i'll update PR with that attachment convention + migration guide. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll try to review before lunch.

maria: assigning now, @kevin @ashley @dom — ping if you need more context.

sre-bot: scheduled canary: 2024-06-18T17:00Z.

maria: noted — will hold off merge until canary gating is green.

kevin: quick logistics Q: do we need a release note entry for the SDKs team? they like heads-up for canonical shapes.

maria: yes, i'll file a short blurb in release notes and message devex.

ashley: Thanks — nice to have the behavior spelled out.

maria: thanks all, i'll push updates to #4123 in a few mins and mark WIP -> ready once tests are in.
